claim: Israel was born from expulsion: the Nakba.

heard.who: Rashid Khalidi, historian, in The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020)
heard.quote: The expulsion then of over half the Arab population of the country, first by Zionist militias and then by the Israeli army, completed the military and political triumph of Zionism.

heard.who: Rashid Khalidi, historian, in The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020)
heard.quote: the ethnic cleansing of Palestine began well before the State of Israel was proclaimed on May 15, 1948

answer: About 700,000 Palestinian Arabs left or were driven from their homes in 1947 to 1949; Britannica says the true figure likely exceeded 700,000. Historians agree on that number and on the fact of expulsions in places, Lydda and Ramle in July 1948 being the clearest. They disagree on the weight of each cause. Some stress fear after fighting and massacre reports, some early departures of wealthy families, some the collapse of Arab leadership, some expulsion as policy. Benny Morris says war, not design, produced the refugee problem; Khalidi says ethnic cleansing; Efraim Karsh puts most blame on Arab leaders. The calls-to-leave story is weak: a researcher found no record of such radio broadcasts. A fair answer does not deny expulsions and does not say they were the only cause.

facts.text: About 700,000 Palestinian Arabs were displaced in 1947 to 1949. Estimates range from about 520,000 to 1,000,000; the figure most often given is around 700,000 or a little more.

sources.title: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
sources.quote: range from about 520,000 to about 1,000,000; there is general consensus, however, that the actual number was more than 600,000 and likely exceeded 700,000

sources.title: The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020)
sources.quote: focused on the return to their homes of the 750,000 or so Palestinian refugees, whose property had been seized by Israel

sources.publisher: MERIP (Middle East Research and Information Project)
sources.title: No More Tears
sources.quote: well over 700,000 Palestinians were made refugees, the majority of them by direct expulsion or the fear of expulsion

facts.text: UN relief counts were lower than that figure: in late 1948 the UN counted 472,000 refugees needing aid, and about 500,000 qualified for relief when UNRWA began in 1950.

sources.title: Assistance to Refugees, supplement to progress report A/648
sources.quote: the figure for Arab refugees must now be revised upwards to 472,000

sources.title: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
sources.quote: some 500,000 Palestinians qualified for relief from the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East

facts.text: In July 1948 Israeli forces expelled the Arab populations of Lydda and Ramle during Operation Dani.

sources.title: The fall of an Arab town in 1948
sources.quote: the surrender, occupation and ultimate expulsion of the Arab residents of al-Ramla, along with the more brutal assault and expulsion of Lydda, were part of the Israeli military's Operation Dani of July 1948

sources.publisher: MERIP (Middle East Research and Information Project)
sources.title: Original Sin
sources.quote: tens of thousands of Palestinian men, women and children were forced out of Lydda and Ramla with the few possessions they could carry

facts.text: Many others left in fear during the fighting. Reports of the Deir Yassin massacre spread, and by mid-May 1948 some 250,000 to 300,000 Palestinian Arabs had left or been expelled.

sources.title: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
sources.quote: word spread among Palestinians of the massacre at Deir Yassin on April 9

sources.title: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
sources.quote: By mid-May, some 250,000-300,000 Palestinian Arabs had left or been expelled from their homes

sources.title: The Origins and Evolution of the Palestine Problem, Part II (1947-1977)
sources.quote: approximately over a quarter of a million of the Arab population have been compelled to leave their homes and emigrate to neighbouring Arab countries

facts.text: Some families left early, before the fighting peaked. Efraim Karsh cites British intelligence from October 1947 that leading Arab figures in Haifa had already sent their families abroad.

sources.title: Were the Palestinians Expelled? (Efraim Karsh)
sources.quote: leading Arab personalities are acting on the assumption that disturbances are near at hand, and have already evacuated their families to neighboring Arab countries

sources.title: The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020)
sources.quote: people fled as news spread of massacres like that on April 9, 1948, in the village of Dayr Yasin near Jerusalem

facts.text: On calls to leave: Karsh reports the Arab Higher Committee evidently ordered women and children removed from Haifa in March 1948. Critics cite Erskine Childers, who found no record of Arab radio broadcasts ordering a general departure and many appeals to stay.

sources.title: Were the Palestinians Expelled? (Efraim Karsh)
sources.quote: in March 1948, the AHC evidently ordered the removal of women and children from Haifa

sources.publisher: MERIP (Middle East Research and Information Project)
sources.title: Original Sin
sources.quote: there was no record of Arab radio broadcasts calling on the Palestinians to leave, there were numerous appeals from Palestinian and Arab officials telling the Palestinians to stay put

facts.text: Palestinian Arab society and leadership were collapsing in the spring of 1948, a point Britannica and Karsh both stress, though Karsh assigns blame to Arab leaders where others do not.

sources.title: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
sources.quote: The Arab front had collapsed, Palestinian Arab communities were being depopulated

sources.title: Efraim Karsh: Takes Israel's New Historians to task
sources.quote: the collapse and dispersion of Palestinian society was largely the responsibility of Palestinian and other Arab leaders, not of the Zionists

facts.text: Historians divide. Benny Morris concluded that war, not design by either side, produced the refugee problem (as summarised by a critic); Karsh says Arab leaders bear most responsibility.

sources.publisher: MERIP (Middle East Research and Information Project)
sources.title: No More Tears
sources.quote: that war and not design, Jewish or Arab, gave birth to the Palestinian refugee problem

sources.title: Efraim Karsh: Takes Israel's New Historians to task
sources.quote: it appears that Morris and other New Historians engaged in systematic falsification of evidence

contested: Causes: Morris (war, not design, with expulsions in places such as Lydda and Ramle), Khalidi (ethnic cleansing as a pattern), Karsh (mainly Arab leadership failure and calls to flee). Ilan Pappe argues the expulsion was planned (Plan Dalet); this card does not quote Pappe because no page of his own words could be read by the checker.

Karsh accuses Morris and other New Historians of misusing evidence; his page states this charge in strong words and the card reports it only as his charge. MERIP's authors criticise Morris's later views. Both are partisan to their own argument.
The numbers: 520,000 to 1,000,000 is Britannica's range. UN relief counts were lower than population estimates, so figures depend on what is counted.

Whether the Lydda and Ramle expulsion was ordered from the top: Morris (as quoted by MERIP) says no decision was taken at the 12 July meeting before Ben-Gurion's reported remark; other writers disagree on how to read it.
not_claimed: This card does not deny that expulsions happened. It says they happened in specific places.
It does not claim all 700,000 were expelled, or that all fled voluntarily.
It does not claim the Arab radio-orders story is proven; the evidence on it is thin and disputed.
It does not address the right of return, property, or who is responsible for the refugees' present status.
